newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Sabena praises Virgin link but more deals to wait.
newsitem.headline: Sabena praises Virgin link but more deals to wait.

text.p: Belgian airline Sabena SA said on Monday its cooperation with Richard Branson's Virgin Express regional airline had taken off successfully but more deals between the two would remain in the hangar for now.

"We have agreed with our pilots association that we cannot outsource more than a certain percentage of our European production," Sabena chief executive officer Paul Reutlinger told a briefing for British journalists.
"So, for the time being, there are no other plans to increase the operation with Virgin Express," he said.

Virgin Express, which was launched in April 1996 after Branson bought 90 percent of EuroBelgian Airlines (EBA), has code-share deals with Sabena for flights between Brussels and London Heathrow, London Gatwick, Rome and Barcelona.

"The bottom line is that it is a very positive operation for Sabena. We have tremendously improved our route profitability. We are transporting more passengers between Brussels and London with less seats offered than before," Reutlinger said.
He said Sabena always lost a lot of money on Brussels-London routes and even more after the opening of the Channel Tunnel and additional cross-channel flights offered by new competitors.

Reutlinger said EBA had been fairly harmless until it was bought by Branson, commenting: "The situation became much more important when with the relatively unknown EBA brand came the very well-known Virgin brand with the charismatic personality of Richard (Branson)."
He said Sabena decided to join Virgin instead of trying to beat it and both airlines had learned from each other.
There was just one hitch in the partnership -- complaints from business passengers about the service on Virgin Express flights.

"We have lost some business class passengers to our competitors because they were not happy with what we are offering on Virgin Express. (But) on the other hand we have tremendously decreased our fares," Reutlinger said.
